## Research question

Which Dodgers hitters project the strongest combination of 2027 availability and offensive performance, and how much does Statcast add beyond traditional batting statistics?

We separate:

- **Playing time:** probability of reaching at least 150 PA.
- **Conditional performance:** next-season wRC+ among hitters who reach 150 PA.

The final holdout is 2026; the application forecast is 2027. The decision focus is the Dodgers roster.

## Data and audit

- FanGraphs all-player batting exports: 2015–2026.
- Baseball Savant season-level Statcast exports: 2015–2026.
- Chadwick Register: stable FanGraphs-to-MLBAM identifier mapping.

The 2015–2025 audit found complete eligible cross-source joins and no duplicate player-season keys. Primary non-2020 retention ranged from approximately 74% to 79%.

```{r audit-table}
audit <- data.frame(
  Check = c("Development seasons", "Primary PA threshold", "2026 holdout", "Primary transitions"),
  Result = c("2015–2025", "150 PA", "Used once for final evaluation", "Eight, excluding 2020")
)
kable(audit, align = c("l", "l"))
```

## EDA: what the data say

2020 is included descriptively but excluded from primary transitions because it was a shortened season with an unusual playing-time environment and tracking-system transition.

For Dodgers roster planning, 150 PA preserves a useful sample while avoiding the noisiest part-time population. A 300 PA screen would focus review on regular players, but it would exclude legitimate role-player forecasts.

## EDA: threshold sensitivity

Retention declines as the prior-season playing-time threshold increases. We keep 150 PA as the primary modeling threshold and use 300 PA only as a stricter review sensitivity.

```{r threshold-chart, fig.height=3.8, out.width='82%'}
thresholds <- data.frame(threshold = c(100, 150, 200, 300), retention = c(.773, .767, .750, .733))
ggplot(thresholds, aes(threshold, retention)) +
  geom_line(color = "#0b1f3a", linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(color = "#d99a2b", size = 3) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(.70, .80)) +
  labs(x = "Prior-season PA threshold", y = "Retention", title = "Dodgers forecast eligibility sensitivity") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 15) +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(8, 16, 8, 24))
```

## Model design

The historical feature set uses PA, wRC+, wOBA, ISO, BB%, and K%. The augmented model adds xwOBA, hard-hit rate, barrel rate, sweet-spot rate, and average exit velocity.

**Frozen choices**

- Historical logistic model for playing-time eligibility.
- Historical + Statcast ridge model for conditional wRC+.
- Fixed XGBoost versions retained as sensitivity analyses.

All imputation and scaling occur inside the model pipeline.

## Model comparison

```{r comparison-table}
comparison <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Historical ridge", "Historical + Statcast ridge", "Historical + Statcast XGBoost"),
  Development_ROC_AUC = c(.808, .809, .807),
  Development_wRC_MAE = c(18.11, 17.63, 17.59)
)
kable(comparison, digits = 3)
```

The Statcast addition helps conditional wRC+ modestly. XGBoost does not provide enough improvement to replace the simpler ridge model.

## 2026 holdout test

```{r holdout-metrics}
holdout_metrics <- data.frame(
  Metric = c("Eligibility accuracy", "Eligibility ROC AUC", "Eligibility Brier", "Conditional wRC+ MAE", "Conditional wRC+ RMSE"),
  Result = c("80.2%", "0.800", "0.146", "17.0", "21.4")
)
kable(holdout_metrics)
```

The holdout visualization showed good broad calibration, with the largest conditional-performance errors among lower-PA players.

## Forecasting 2027

The selected models were refit through 2026 and applied to Dodgers hitters with at least 150 PA in 2026.

The strict review screen requires:

- Eligibility probability ≥ 0.50.
- Predicted wRC+ ≥ 110.
- Predicted wRC+ at least 10 points above 2026 wRC+.

The shortlist below is intended for Dodgers roster and player-development discussion, not as an automatic transaction recommendation.

## Dodgers forecast shortlist

```{r dodgers-table}
dodgers_show <- dodgers[1:min(8, nrow(dodgers)), c("Name", "pa_fg", "wrc_plus", "predicted_wrc_plus", "predicted_eligibility_probability")]
names(dodgers_show) <- c("Player", "2026 PA", "2026 wRC+", "2027 predicted wRC+", "Eligibility probability")
kable(dodgers_show, digits = 1)
```

## Dodgers forecast chart

```{r dodgers-chart}
dodgers_plot <- dodgers[1:min(8, nrow(dodgers)), ]
dodgers_plot$Name <- factor(dodgers_plot$Name, levels = rev(dodgers_plot$Name))
ggplot(dodgers_plot, aes(predicted_wrc_plus, Name)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#0b1f3a") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", predicted_wrc_plus)), hjust = -0.15, size = 4) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 140)) +
  labs(x = "Predicted 2027 wRC+", y = NULL, title = "Dodgers: selected 2027 forecasts") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```

## Dodgers player review priorities

The 150 PA threshold is the eligibility target used throughout the project. The review screen emphasizes predicted wRC+ of at least 110 and an improvement of at least 10 points over 2026.

```{r review-table}
review <- dodgers[1:min(4, nrow(dodgers)), c("Name", "pa_fg", "wrc_plus", "predicted_wrc_plus", "predicted_eligibility_probability", "predicted_wrc_plus_lift_vs_2026")]
names(review) <- c("Player", "2026 PA", "2026 wRC+", "Pred. 2027 wRC+", "Eligible", "Lift")
kable(review, digits = 1, align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"))
```

These are Dodgers roster-planning priorities, not automatic acquisition recommendations. Add health, roster status, defensive role, and expected playing time during baseball review.

## Limitations

- Only five expanding development folds were available.
- 2020 is not exchangeable with a normal season.
- Statcast missingness is non-random and flagged in the forecast output.
- No age, injury, contract, park, role, or roster-context variables are modeled.
- 2027 outcomes are not yet available.
- Forecasts are predictive and associative, not causal.
